messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: "﻿invalid factor level, NAs generated" (plotmatrix)
parts:
Hi Ista:

To allay your concerns, plotmatrix() can handle factors:  :)

library(ggplot2)
str(OrchardSprays)
plotmatrix(OrchardSprays)

The problem with PY's data set is that  cu.summary contains missing values in both Reliability (ordered factor) and Mileage (numeric):
> sapply(cu.summary, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
      Price     Country Reliability     Mileage        Type
          0           0          32          57           0

I tried making Reliability an ordered factor with NA as a valid level, but still got warning messages re missing values with mileage, so it appears, at least on the surface, to be an NA handling problem. In cu.summary, we have the following table of the number of missing values per line:

library(rpart)
table(apply(cu.summary, 1, function(x) sum(is.na(x))))

 0  1  2
49 47 21

i.e., 21 observations have NA values for both Reliability and Mileage, 47 observations have one NA and 49 have no NAs.

From the help page of plotmatrix, Hadley's warning was quite direct:

plotmatrix {ggplot2}R Documentation

Code to create a scatterplot matrix (experimental)

Description

Crude experimental scatterplot matrix


Fortunately, there are a number of useful scatterplot matrix functions in R, which one can find through

library(sos)
findFn('scatterplot matrix')

if one needs an immediate solution. To investigate missing values in particular, package VIM has a couple of neat little functions.

Dennis
